prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
The document sets out a programme across Brexit, the economy, public services, climate, rights, democracy, and foreign policy. Key proposals include:

Brexit and democratic reform
- Stop Brexit by revoking Article 50 with a governing mandate; otherwise support a public vote with an option to remain. Retain freedom of movement and secure a projected £50bn “Remain Bonus” to invest in services.
- Replace First-Past-the-Post with proportional representation (STV); votes at 16; automatic voter registration; oppose voter ID; reform the House of Lords; stricter transparency on political advertising and lobbying; citizens’ assemblies; major devolution within a federal UK and a written constitution.

Economy, work, business
- Invest £130bn in infrastructure (transport, energy, schools, hospitals, housing) plus a £50bn regional rebalancing fund and a Green Investment Bank (£5bn initial capital).
- A “Skills Wallet” of £10,000 per adult for lifelong learning; expand apprenticeships; national skills strategies.
- Corporate tax at 20%; overhaul business rates into a land value-based levy; tougher action on avoidance by multinationals and tech giants.
- Modernise employment rights: a new “dependent contractor” status; flexible working from day one; fair gig-economy rules; stronger enforcement; living wage review.

Education and childcare
- Free, high-quality childcare from nine months for working parents and for all children aged 2–4 (35 hours, 48 weeks); increased early years funding; expand Children’s Centres.
- Reverse school cuts; hire 20,000 teachers; repair school buildings; boost SEND support; scrap SATs; replace Ofsted; broader “curriculum for life.”
- Free school meals for all primary pupils and for secondary pupils on Universal Credit; stronger mental health support in schools.
- Restore maintenance grants; expand Further Education funding; student mental health standards.

Health and social care
- Raise £7bn annually via a 1p income tax rise, ringfenced for health and care; £10bn capital investment.
- Plan a dedicated Health and Care Tax; cross-party convention; independent funding watchdog.
- Mental health parity: new waiting-time standards; expanded talking therapies; perinatal and crisis care; implement Mental Health Act reforms.
- Address workforce shortages (GPs, nurses, allied staff); ethical international recruitment; integrate health and social care; regulate care professions; enhanced support for unpaid carers.

Climate, energy, nature, transport
- Net zero by 2045; at least 80% renewable electricity by 2030; ban fracking; £6bn+ per year to insulate homes; zero‑carbon new buildings from 2021; accelerate zero‑carbon heat.
- Nature Act with binding targets; plant 60m trees annually; restore habitats; circular economy and Zero‑Waste law; deposits on containers; ban non‑recyclable single-use plastics.
- Clean Air Act; all new cars and small vans electric by 2030; extend Ultra-Low Emission Zones; electrify rail by 2035; freeze commuter rail fares for a parliament; restore bus routes; major cycling/walking investment.

Housing, welfare, communities, justice
- Build 300,000 homes a year including 100,000 social; zero‑carbon standards; Rent to Own; longer tenancies; licensing and higher standards for renters; act on second homes.
- Overhaul Universal Credit: cut first payment wait to five days; remove two‑child limit and benefit cap; end punitive sanctions; increase Local Housing Allowance; end bedroom tax.
- End rough sleeping within five years via “somewhere safe to stay” duty and support packages.
- Public health approach to violence: restore community policing; invest in youth services; reduce reoffending with rehabilitation, presumption against short sentences, and better through‑the‑gate support.

Rights, migration, asylum
- Protect the Human Rights Act and ECHR; restore Legal Aid; halt police facial recognition; modernise family law; strengthen equality law; tackle hate crime; BSL Act; end period poverty.
- Replace the “hostile environment”; 28‑day limit on immigration detention; move visa policymaking out of the Home Office; flexible work/student visas; fairer fees; right to work for asylum seekers after three months; expand resettlement, family reunion, and integration support.

Foreign policy and defence
- Support multilateralism (UN, NATO); maintain 0.7% aid; climate leadership; tighter arms export controls (including suspending sales to Saudi Arabia); Magnitsky‑style sanctions.
- Parliamentary votes on military action; support Iran deal; recognise Palestine; back Ukraine; expand cyber defence; maintain a minimum nuclear deterrent with reduced posture; improve support for service personnel and veterans.
